name: Tolperisone + Diclofenac Sodium
meta: Tolperisone 150 mg + Diclofenac sodium 50 mg (strength not stated in product list –
Tolperisone Hydrochloride: Centrally acting muscle relaxant (non-sedating); Diclofenac (Sodium / Potassium): Non-selective NSAID (phenylacetic acid derivative)
Tolperisone Hydrochloride: M03BX04; Diclofenac (Sodium / Potassium): M01AB05
Schedule H – prescription only; Diclofenac (Sodium / Potassium): Schedule H – prescription only
sections: White crystalline powder (hydrochloride), very soluble in water.
Sodium salt: white to slightly yellowish, slightly hygroscopic crystalline powder, sparingly soluble in water.

Tolperisone Hydrochloride: In use since the 1960s; after a 2012 EMA referral, use in the EU was restricted to adults with post-stroke spasticity because of hypersensitivity reactions. First approval/introduction: Developed in Hungary in the 1960s (Gedeon Richter). Diclofenac (Sodium / Potassium): One of the most widely used NSAIDs worldwide; on the WHO List of Essential Medicines. First approval/introduction: Synthesised 1973 (Sallmann and Pfister, Ciba-Geigy); US approval 1988.
Tolperisone 150 mg + Diclofenac sodium 50 mg (strength not stated in product list –
Non-sedating muscle relaxation with NSAID analgesia – helps patients remain active while recovering.

Tolperisone Hydrochloride Blocks voltage-gated sodium and calcium channels in the brainstem reticular formation and spinal cord, inhibiting polysynaptic reflexes; relieves muscle spasm and spasticity without significant sedation. Receptor / target profile: Blocks voltage-gated sodium and calcium channels in the brainstem reticular formation and spinal cord, inhibiting polysynaptic reflexes without sedation.

Diclofenac (Sodium / Potassium) Inhibits COX-1 and COX-2 reducing prostaglandin synthesis; potassium salt gives faster absorption and onset. Receptor / target profile: Inhibits COX-1 and COX-2 (partially COX-2 selective); also blocks voltage-dependent sodium channels and acid-sensing ion channels.
Summary: Well absorbed; Tmax 0.5–1 h (ER prolongs); high first-pass metabolism (CYP2D6, CYP2C19). Half-life ~2.5 h.
Hepatic – CYP2C9 (main), CYP2C8, CYP3A4; glucuronidation and sulfation
Summary: Complete absorption; ~50% first-pass. Tmax 0.5–1 h (potassium), 2 h (sodium EC). >99% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP2C9. Half-life 1–2 h.
Painful musculoskeletal conditions with muscle spasm – low back pain, neck pain, sprains
One tablet twice daily after meals

Tolperisone Hydrochloride: Take after meals with water (food increases bioavailability).
Diclofenac (Sodium / Potassium): Take after food or with milk; avoid alcohol (GI bleeding).
Diclofenac (Sodium / Potassium): BP, renal function, LFTs and CBC on prolonged use; signs of GI bleeding.
Tolperisone Hydrochloride: Ataxia, hypotonia, seizures, dyspnoea. Supportive care. Diclofenac (Sodium / Potassium): GI bleeding, renal failure, hepatotoxicity, seizures. Supportive care.
Stop and seek help if rash, swelling or breathing difficulty
Do not combine with other painkillers containing NSAIDs
Report black stools, vomiting blood, chest pain, swelling
Use for the shortest time needed
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
